capture.clock_start: 2026-10-08T22:40:00+08:00 = the first evening after the rc2 build (SHOTS.md: "an evening after the build time"). The static runtime clamps its clock to the build time (createClock, buildAtMs = 2026-10-08 04:18 +08:00), so rc1's 2026-10-07 22:40 would print 04:19 on screen. capture.playback_speed: virtual time advances 16 ms per frame and the files are 60 fps: playback is 4 % slower than real time (62.5 -> 60), as in every clip made with this rig; all times here are video times (frame / 60)
capture.pointer: no cursor: the rig's doodle tap ring (yellow ring, ink outline, pink offset; 30 frames) marks each UI tap; camera glides are started with a plain element.click() on the product's own nav button / person label (no ring)
capture.three_d_resolution: the product renders its 3D canvas at 2x CSS (its own cap), so in the 3840x2160 master the 3D layer is a 1.33x upscale while all DOM/type is native 4K; punch-ins on the 3D up to 1.5x of the 1080 frame stay at native 3D resolution
capture.ai_timing: the on-device AI runs in real time while the virtual clock is stepped frame by frame, so the chip 「AI 判断：人海」 lands a few frames after the tap in the video; the result itself is the model's real answer
capture.text_audit: before the first frame of every clip and every 12 frames while recording: document.body.innerText (rendered text only) + title/aria-label/placeholder/alt/value of rendered elements grepped for 示例|虚构|本页|演示|自动回复|不是真人|没有服务器|只存在这个浏览器|模拟|本地体验版|在线访问|等待本人回应; a hit fails the take. The 3D canvas (stage sign, prints) cannot be grepped and was checked by eye on the stills and contact sheet.

encoding.master: H.264 High, CRF 15, preset slow, tune animation, yuv420p, BT.709 primaries/transfer/matrix, limited range, 60 fps CFR, +faststart, no audio, 3840x2160
encoding.edit: same settings, 1920x1080, Lanczos downscale (accurate_rnd, full_chroma_int) made from the same lossless PNG frames in the same ffmpeg pass (not from the H.264 master)

conventions.time: seconds of video time from the first frame of the file (frame / 60)
conventions.boxes: [x, y, w, h] in master pixels (3840x2160); divide by 2 for the 1080 edit copy
conventions.taps: frame = the ring appears (mousedown); dom_click_frame = frame + 3 (mouseup, the product reacts from here)
conventions.beat_grid: taps that follow each other are placed on a 123 BPM grid (Flipping In): beat k at frame zero + round(k * 29.268); other tempos: re-time by cutting between taps
conventions.people: per person: label box in master px; the figure stands below the label stem (about 80 x 170 CSS px = 213 x 453 master px at the overview camera)
conventions.vs_rc1: per clip: frame counts, tap frames and every mark box that moved more than 4 master px (or was added/removed) compared with the rc1 manifest; scenes that address rc1 footage by source pixels should re-read these

Product behaviour, not a capture fault: while the camera heads to the photo wall or to one person, the product hides the other figures and the overlay labels/cards at once (first frame of the glide) and shows a small 「正在靠近」 chip; glides back to the overview show everyone from their first frame. In D-02 the vanish frames are 8.00 s (cast) and 17.00 s (all but 阿遥).

Product behaviour: the photos view frames four photos close (one row) and five photos wider (two rows), so D-03a -> D-03b is a re-frame plus the new polaroid; in D-03s the re-frame happens on the frame the panel switches to the wall (6.50 s).
The desktop header shows the product's 「音乐探索 ↗」 pill (entry to the Doodle Music Map) in every room frame; the map itself is not part of these takes. Its box is 'headerMusicMap' in the D-02 marks.

Playback is 4 % slower than real time (rig: 16 ms of virtual time per 60 fps frame). Waits shown uncut: 阿遥 accepting the exchange and 小满 accepting the greeting / replying take their real (seeded) times on the virtual clock.

The on-device AI answers in real time while the virtual clock is stepped: 「AI 判断：人海」 appears 1 frame after the DOM click in D-03s (2.617 s). The answer is the model's real output on 「人海那张」. rc2 fetches the model off the main thread, so the rig now confirms the download from the prefix server's own request log.

Holds change on the product's line boil (every 8.9 frames on the virtual clock = 6.7 boils per second); between boils most frames differ by 1-4 pixels of 3D render noise (invisible). The edit's PUSH keeps holds moving as the storyboard asks.
Tap rings are the rig's doodle ring (yellow, ink outline, pink offset, 30 frames); there is no pointer arrow anywhere. Camera glides are started without a ring.
problems: None blocking.
